task_2.title: Restore production as Flask's default environment
task_2.description: This update corrects Flask's default environment selection so applications run as production when FLASK_ENV is not set, matching prior behavior and avoiding an incorrect development default. It also stops showing the deprecated app.env value in the flask shell banner.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that a Flask application defaults to production mode when no FLASK_ENV value is provided, and ensure deprecated environment metadata is not surfaced in the interactive shell banner.

expectation.grounded: When a Flask app initializes its default config and the FLASK_ENV environment variable is unset or empty, config['ENV'] must resolve to 'production' rather than 'development'. The deprecated app.env attribute should remain deprecated, and flask shell startup output should no longer display the current environment via app.env.
expectation.conceptual: Applications that do not explicitly opt into a different environment should behave as production deployments by default. Interactive CLI output should avoid presenting deprecated environment state to users.

constraints.grounded: If FLASK_ENV is explicitly provided, its value must continue to populate the application's ENV setting. Existing debug-flag behavior must remain unchanged. The change must not reintroduce app.env as part of normal flask shell banner output.
constraints.conceptual: Only the unset-default environment behavior should change; explicit environment configuration and unrelated runtime settings should continue to behave as before. The deprecation status of the old environment attribute should be preserved.

behavior: A Flask application created without FLASK_ENV set now exposes ENV as production by default.
An empty FLASK_ENV value is treated the same as an unset value for choosing the default environment.
Applications no longer default to development solely because FLASK_ENV is absent.
The flask shell banner no longer includes the application's environment value sourced from the deprecated app.env attribute.
acceptance_criteria: When a Flask application starts with FLASK_ENV unset, it should report its ENV configuration as production.
When a Flask application starts with FLASK_ENV set to a specific value, it should continue using that value for ENV.
When launching flask shell, the startup banner should identify the app and instance path without showing the deprecated environment field.

When upgrading from 2.2.1 to 2.2.2 without changing deployment configuration, an app that previously appeared to default to development because FLASK_ENV was unset should instead default to production.

task_1.title: Require Werkzeug 2.2.2 and remove duplicate development server warnings
task_1.description: Flask now depends on Werkzeug 2.2.2 so applications pick up the router and header parsing correctness fixes from that release, and Flask no longer prints its own duplicate development-server warning because Werkzeug already provides it.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from Flask 2.2.1 to 2.2.2 requires Werkzeug 2.2.2 or newer, so users receive the corresponding router and header parsing fixes, and ensure that starting the development server no longer shows a duplicate development-server warning.

expectation.grounded: Flask 2.2.2 must declare a minimum dependency of Werkzeug >= 2.2.2. Users running the Flask development server through the CLI, such as `flask run`, should receive Werkzeug's development-server warning without an additional Flask-emitted duplicate warning. By requiring Werkzeug 2.2.2, Flask applications should also inherit the routing and header parsing correctness fixes shipped in that Werkzeug release.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, applications should run against a Werkzeug version that contains the needed correctness fixes, and the development server startup output should be cleaner by showing the safety warning only once while preserving normal startup information.

constraints.grounded: Do not allow environments with Werkzeug versions below 2.2.2 to satisfy Flask's install requirements. Do not suppress Werkzeug's own development-server warning. Preserve the normal Flask CLI startup banner behavior, including identifying the served app when that information is available.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should tighten the dependency floor without requiring users to change their application code, and it should remove redundant warning output without hiding essential startup details.

behavior: Flask's package dependency now requires Werkzeug version 2.2.2 or newer.
Upgrading Flask to 2.2.2 causes applications to run with the Werkzeug 2.2.2 router and header parsing fixes rather than older 2.2.x behavior.
Starting the Flask development server no longer emits a second Flask-specific development-server warning banner.
The Flask CLI still announces the served application when the app import path is known.
acceptance_criteria: When Flask 2.2.2 is installed, dependency resolution should require Werkzeug 2.2.2 or newer.
When a user starts the development server through the Flask CLI, the startup output should contain only one development-server warning rather than duplicate warnings from both Flask and Werkzeug.
When an application upgrades from Flask 2.2.1 to 2.2.2, routing and header parsing behavior should reflect the fixes provided by Werkzeug 2.2.2 without additional configuration.
When the Flask CLI knows which application is being served, it should still display that application information during startup.
